correction: DONE holds for the performance cost. A lone pane now passes its React key on, so desktop thread switches reuse ChatView, the composer and the Lexical editor, and useDeferredValue has an initial value again. The auditor's 'fixDefects: None seen' is wrong. Reusing the ChatView brings back cross-thread state leaks that the per-thread remount used to hide. (1) The Lexical undo history is shared across threads, so Cmd+Z after a switch writes the previous thread's prompt into the new thread's draft. I reproduced this with lexical@0.50 registerHistory: a controlled swap from 'draft for thread A' to '' followed by UNDO_COMMAND gives back 'draft for thread A' with the 'historic' tag, and OnChangePlugin does not filter that tag. (2) The send pipeline runs async continuations that write to instance-wide state (sendInFlightRef, promptRef, the local dispatch snapshot, the composer handle). When the user switches threads while a send is in flight, those writes now land on the new thread. The ChatPanes browser test the auditor cites mounts a stub textarea, not ChatView, so it cannot catch any of this.
summary: The performance fix is in. In ChatPanes, nextPaneReactKeys hands a lone pane's React key to the next lone thread, so ChatView, ChatComposer and the Lexical editor survive a desktop thread switch. useDeferredValue(activeThreadIdRaw, null), plus the worktree-launch exception, paints chrome and composer first and mounts the timeline in a transition. The proposal said reusing the instance would require resetting thread-scoped state, and that is only partly done. ChatView and ChatComposer reset their useState on a thread switch. Two kinds of thread-scoped state are still shared. First, the composer's Lexical HistoryPlugin stack: undo after a switch puts thread A's prompt into thread B's draft. Second, the send pipeline's instance-wide refs and callbacks: a send from A that is still in flight when the user switches can leave B stuck as busy, drop B's sends without feedback, or, if A's send fails, lose A's prompt or load A's text into B's prompt ref.

evidence.note: If reuseLonePane is set and both the previous and next root are a lone thread, the next thread inherits the previous React key.

nextLayoutMotion passes reuseLonePane = enabled, and the <section> is keyed by layoutMotion.reactKeys. The discarded render with stale keys is replaced by React's setState-during-render re-render, so it never commits.

Both desktop branches use <ChatPanes threadRef> with the default enabled=true. The frozen phone tier passes enabled={false} and still remounts. The route loader is synchronous, so a thread switch never shows the pendingComponent.

useDeferredValue(activeThreadIdRaw, continuesWorktreeLaunch ? activeThreadIdRaw : null). continuesWorktreeLaunch is computed once per instance and only feeds the initial value, which React ignores after mount, so it does no harm.

Thread-scoped resets for the header popovers, provider-status dismissal, the PR dialog, scroll and live-follow, the overview, optimistic messages, resetLocalDispatch and the pending branch. ChatComposer.tsx:1362-1368 resets the cursor and trigger on a draftId/activeThreadId change.

DEFECT: the controlled value sync calls editor.update with no history tag, so every thread switch pushes the previous thread's editor state onto the shared HistoryPlugin undo stack. Nothing dispatches CLEAR_HISTORY_COMMAND, and the editor is keyed only by an HMR constant. Undo after a switch restores thread A's text. OnChangePlugin, which ignores only history-merge, then calls onChange, and ChatComposer writes that text into thread B's draft. Reproduced with lexical@0.50 registerHistory: [["draft for thread A",""],["",""],["","historic"],["draft for thread A","historic"]].

DEFECT (race): just before thread.turn.start, which comes after the uploads, the Claude resume review and the settings round trip, the pipeline calls beginLocalDispatch again. That snapshot is taken from activeThreadRef.current. After a switch, this is thread B. B's turn and session state do not change, so the server never acknowledges the snapshot. On success, executeChatSendTurn.ts:781-783 does not reset it. B stays isSendBusy (runSend returns at ChatView.tsx:4423-4430) and shows a working timer until the user switches threads again.

DEFECT (race): sendInFlightRef is shared by all threads the instance shows, while thread A's send pipeline is in flight. Enter in thread B returns silently during that window. The composerSubmitGuard at ChatView.tsx:4720 is already keyed by thread, which shows the intended design.

DEFECT (failure after a switch): rollbackSendTurn checks the live instance refs, which now hold thread B's content. If B's composer has text, thread A's failed prompt is never restored to A's draft, so it is lost: A's draft was cleared at send and the optimistic message is removed. If B is empty, refs.promptRef.current is set to A's prompt and resetCursorState runs on B's composer. B's prompt state does not change, so ChatComposer's promptRef sync effect does not re-run, and the next runSend in B reads promptForSend = promptRef.current (ChatView.tsx:4446). The plan follow-up continuation (ChatView.tsx:4888-4906) also calls setPlanSidebarOpen/resetLocalDispatch on whatever thread is showing.
The reuse test renders a stub <textarea>, not ChatView, so it does not exercise composer, editor or send-pipeline state across a switch.

fixDefects: 1) Cross-thread undo: the reused Lexical editor (ComposerPromptEditor.tsx:1454-1497 controlled sync, HistoryPlugin at :1695) keeps one undo stack for every thread. After switching A->B, Cmd+Z in B's composer, which the switch effect at ChatView.tsx:3309-3317 auto-focuses, restores A's prompt, and OnChangePlugin writes it into B's persisted draft. That can send A's text to B's agent, possibly on a different machine or project. This is deterministic and needs only an undo. 2) Send continuations hit the newly shown thread. beginLocalDispatch at sendEngine.ts:402 runs after the awaits and can snapshot thread B, which leaves B busy and blocks its sends (useLocalDispatchState.ts:43-53, 93). sendInFlightRef (ChatView.tsx:829) silently drops B's sends while A's send is in flight. On a failed A send, rollbackSendTurn (executeChatSendTurn.ts:340-354) either loses A's prompt, when B has content, or loads A's prompt into the shared promptRef behind B's empty composer. These need a switch while a send is in flight: likely with image uploads, settings changes, a Claude resume review or a slow hosted relay, rare for plain text sends. Before 141d441c7, when ChatView was also unkeyed, these hazards existed too; the per-thread remount that the fix removed is what had been hiding them. Minor, cosmetic: ChatComposer's isStashPickerOpen and isComposerModelPickerOpen (ChatComposer.tsx:919, 923) are not reset on a switch.
implementationSketch: A) Undo history: give ComposerPromptEditor a `historyScope` prop. ChatComposer passes scopedThreadKey(composerDraftTarget) or the draftId. In ComposerPromptEditorInner's controlled-sync useLayoutEffect, when historyScope changes, run the rewrite with editor.update(fn, { tag: HISTORIC_TAG }) and then editor.dispatchCommand(CLEAR_HISTORY_COMMAND, undefined). Optional: keep a small LRU Map<scope, HistoryState> and pass <HistoryPlugin externalHistoryState={...}> so each thread keeps its own undo stack. Test: a ComposerPromptEditor browser test that renders value 'A' with scope a, rerenders value '' with scope b, presses Mod+Z, and asserts that onChange never receives 'A' and the editor stays empty. B) Thread-bound send continuations, as one shared helper rather than per-call patches: (1) useLocalDispatchState: store the thread key in LocalDispatchSnapshot; make beginLocalDispatch take the send's thread key and ignore it when that key is not the active one, and treat a snapshot whose key differs from the active thread as null. (2) Replace sendInFlightRef with a per-thread-key Set, the same shape as createThreadSubmitGuard (ChatView.logic.ts:462), and check the active key in runSend, onSubmitPlanFollowUp, onImplementPlanInNewThread and startGoalTurnRef. (3) executeChatSendTurn: capture the send's draft target, and before rollback or restore compare it with a getActiveDraftTarget() dep. When they differ, decide whether to restore from the target's draft in the composer draft store, not from the live refs; write only to that target; skip refs and composerHandle. (4) Guard the setPlanSidebarOpen and resetLocalDispatch calls in the plan follow-up continuation the same way. Tests: extend executeChatSendTurn.test.ts with a switch before failure (B's refs have content, then B's refs are empty) and assert A's draft is restored and B's refs are untouched. Add a useLocalDispatchState unit test for a begin after the key changes. Add a ChatView browser test: hold dispatchCommand pending, navigate A->B, resolve, assert B is not busy and B can send.
decisionReason: Client-only correctness fixes inside the web composer and send pipeline. They touch no E2EE, auth, hosted lifecycle ownership or Hub protocol. Keeping a per-thread undo history versus clearing it on a switch is a small UX choice an implementer can make.
